sentences.text: Bonapartenykus is an extinct alvarezsauroid dinosaur, a member of the Alvarezsauroidea clade, that lived within the class Reptilia.
This dinosaur is distinguished by specific anatomical features, including laminae on its vertebrae, a deflected coracoid with grooves, and a concave triangular surface on the distal pubic shaft.

Its vertebrae possess a deeply concave cranial articular surface that might be procoelous, while the coracoid is extremely elongate with an acute end that restricted its articulation with the sternum.
Based on its skeletal structure, Bonapartenykus likely had a flat and wide breast, and the distal end of the pubic shaft features a rounded pubic boot on its rear margin.
It possessed a very short and robust tibia with a shaft bowed towards the sides.
Bonapartenykus is the largest known member of the Alvarezsauroidea clade, with an estimated length of 2.5 to 3.3 meters and a weight of 43 to 72 kilograms.
The species was found with two incomplete eggs and eggshells belonging to the oogenus Arriagadoolithus, which were unique enough to be named and classified in the new oofamily Arriagadoolithidae.

The genus Bonapartenykus was named in 2012 by Federico L. Agnolin, Jaime E. Powell, Fernando E. Novas, and Martin Kundrát, honoring Argentine paleontologist José F. Bonaparte by combining his name with the Latin word for claw.

A partial skeleton associated with eggs was collected from approximately 30 square meters of fluvial sandstone in northwestern Patagonia, Argentina, where the holotype specimen includes a mid-dorsal vertebra, scapulocoracoids, leg bones, and two eggs found less than 20 centimeters from the skeleton.
There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Bonapartenykus, and Meso et al. (2026) published a redescription of the anatomy of the holotype specimen of Bonapartenykus ultimus.

Agnolin et al. (2012) originally classified Bonapartenykus as a member of the clade Patagonykinae within the family Alvarezsauridae, making it the sister taxon to Patagonykus, though Xu et al. (2018) recovered it as a basal alvarezsauroid that was not part of the Alvarezsauridae family and was more primitive than Patagonykus and Achillesaurus.
However, Meso et al. (2025) re-analyzed the bones and recovered Bonapartenykus as a patagonykine within the Alvarezsauridae, supporting the earlier classification by Agnolin et al. (2012).
Bonapartenykus is an extinct alvarezsauroid dinosaur that lived in the Late Cretaceous of the Allen Formation in Argentina, and its parent group is Alvarezsauroidea.

Bonapartenykus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago, and fossils are found in the upper Allen Formation, dated to the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
It lived alongside diverse fauna including sauropods like Bonatitan, hadrosaurids like Bonapartesaurus, the abelisaurid theropod Quilmesaurus, and the pterosaur Aerotitan.

The classification of Bonapartenykus remains debated, with some analyses placing it as a basal alvarezsauroid outside the family Alvarezsauridae, while others support its placement within the Patagonykinae subclade.
